## R1 repair — the mirror no longer refuses its own prior write (review candidate `5743eb15`, finding R1)

**Task.** `mirrorFinalizationArtifacts` refused `content_diverged` on its OWN second call when the
main-side run record had legitimately advanced since a prior successful mirror and the worktree copy
was left untouched — the transaction reading state it manufactured itself as an operator conflict.
tdd-1054-finalize's RED landed in `test-ledger-compare.js` (leg `(f)`, 8 new assertions) and
`test-issue-1054-ledger-guard.js` (legs R1a-R1d, 18 new assertions across all four editions);
confirmed RED before touching production code (ledger-compare: 1 failure at f1; ledger-guard: 18
failures, 49 passed).

**Design implemented (matches the design of record from the dispatch exactly):**
- `compareLedgers(srcText, destText, opts)` in `scripts/kaola-workflow-ledger-compare.js` gained a
  third, optional `{ priorDigest }` argument. When dest's CURRENT bytes hash (sha256) to exactly
  `priorDigest`, the verdict is `{ safe: true, reason: 'prior_mirror' }`. This arm is checked AFTER
  `first_sync` and `identical` (never overrides either) and falls through to the ordinary
  `content_diverged`/`diff_unavailable` comparison whenever dest does not hash to the supplied
  digest — an independent edit, a wrong/garbage digest, or no digest supplied at all reproduce
  today's exact pre-R1 behavior.
- `mirrorFinalizationArtifacts` in `scripts/kaola-workflow-claim.js` (and both forge hand-ports)
  reads `.cache/mirror-digest.json` from the DEST project folder before comparing (missing or
  unparsable JSON degrades to `undefined` priorDigest — never throws), passes it through to
  `compareLedgers`, and — only after the merge-copy itself has already succeeded — writes/updates
  that file mapping `mission-list.md` to the sha256 of the bytes it just copied. The write is
  best-effort (swallow-on-error): the mirror already succeeded by that point, and losing the receipt
  only costs the NEXT run the leniency, never a silent bypass.
- Measured first, as asked: `mergeCopyDir` (the Step-8a copy primitive) is a MERGE-copy that walks
  only the SOURCE tree — it can never delete or clobber a dest-only file, so a `mirror-digest.json`
  that exists only in dest (main never writes one) is safe from every subsequent mirror call by
  construction; no `keepExisting`/exclusion entry was needed for it.
- **Archive decision (recorded inline in both the code comment and here, as asked):** the receipt is
  left **unexcluded** from the archive. Once a project is archived, `mirrorFinalizationArtifacts`
  short-circuits to `skipped_post_archive` before ever reading the file again, so a copy sitting in
  an archived project is simply inert — the same shape as `.cache/chain-receipt.json` or
  `.cache/run-gaps.json`, both also TREE_BOUND/JSON evidence that already rides into the archive
  unexcluded via `copyDir`. Actively dropping it would require its own carve-out through
  `verifyArchiveComplete`'s "every file the source holds must reach the destination" completeness
  proof — the same seam `SINK_JOURNAL_RE` occupies for `sink-receipt.json`/`sink-fallback.json`, a
  DIFFERENT family (those are 'forge' records disposed at terminal success because a live one left
  behind would misdescribe unfinished sink progress as current publication state; this file
  describes nothing an archive reader could misread). That is real machinery the finding does not
  warrant, so none was built — enforcement point is simply "there is none."
- `KERNEL_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY` in `scripts/kaola-workflow-adaptive-schema.js` gained one literal row —
  `['.cache/mirror-digest.json', 'record', 'evidence', 'script', …]` — placed after the
  `.cache/run-gaps.json` row (both are `.cache/*.json` evidence, so ordering relative to each other
  is inert; it precedes the two broad bands as required). `docs/workflow-state-contract.md`'s
  Layer-0 table got the matching row at the same index, matcher/ruling/record/writer verbatim-equal
  (the `Why` prose column is not part of the machine-checked equality, per
  `test-kernel-conformance.js`'s `partB()`).

**Verification tier:** tests-green — both RED suites now pass in full, plus the full requested list.

**Files changed:**
- `scripts/kaola-workflow-ledger-compare.js` — `compareLedgers` gains `opts.priorDigest`; new
  `sha256Hex` helper; `crypto` required.
- `scripts/kaola-workflow-claim.js` — `mirrorFinalizationArtifacts`: reads/writes the digest;
  new `MIRROR_DIGEST_REL`, `sha256Hex`, `readMirrorDigest`, `writeMirrorDigest` helpers placed beside
  `FINALIZE_MIRROR_TREE_BOUND`.
- `plugins/kaola-workflow-gitlab/scripts/kaola-gitlab-workflow-claim.js`,
  `plugins/kaola-workflow-gitea/scripts/kaola-gitea-workflow-claim.js` — identical hand-ported edits.
- `scripts/kaola-workflow-adaptive-schema.js` — one new `KERNEL_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY` row.
- `docs/workflow-state-contract.md` — matching Layer-0 table row.
- Propagated: `plugins/kaola-workflow/scripts/kaola-workflow-claim.js` (codex byte-copy),
  `plugins/{kaola-workflow,kaola-workflow-gitlab,kaola-workflow-gitea}/scripts/kaola-workflow-ledger-compare.js`

## R1 follow-up — `probeFinalizeMirror` (`finalize --check`'s read-only twin) must agree with the mirror

**Task.** `probeFinalizeMirror` predicts what the Step-8a mirror will do without performing it, and
still called `compareLedgers(src, dest)` with no `priorDigest` — so `--check` predicted
`sync_failed`/`mirror_sync_failed` for exactly the main-advanced/worktree-untouched pair the R1 fix
above now lets the real transaction proceed through as `prior_mirror`. The prediction had stopped
agreeing with what the transaction actually does.

tdd-1054-finalize's RED landed as two new legs in `test-issue-1054-ledger-guard.js` — R1e (four
editions: `--check` must report `checks.mirror === 'ready'` and drop `mirror_sync_failed` from
`reasons` for the prior_mirror-safe pair, read-only — neither copy nor the receipt itself may
change) and R1f (a hand-edited worktree copy must still predict `sync_failed`, mirroring R1b).
Confirmed RED first: 8 failures / 88 passed.

**Fix.** `probeFinalizeMirror` in `scripts/kaola-workflow-claim.js` (and both forge hand-ports) now
calls the SAME `readMirrorDigest(destDir)` helper `mirrorFinalizationArtifacts` uses — shared, not
duplicated, exactly as asked — and passes its `{ priorDigest }` through to `compareLedgers`, read-only
(the function never writes; `readMirrorDigest` was already read-only by construction, so nothing new
needed to be built for that half). Missing/corrupt receipt degrades to no `priorDigest`, identical to
the mirror's own degradation.

**Verification tier:** tests-green.
